title: Janmashtami
description: Sri Krishna Janmashtami event is celebrated worldwide with great devotion and variegated festivities. There are splendid decorations, chanting of auspicious mantras, performances of melodious kirtans, bhajans, dramas and display of video shows, narrations of wonderful pastimes of the Lord etc.

title: Nandotsav
description: Nandotsav is a festival celebrated the day after the festival Janmashtami, which celebrates the Lord Krishna's birth.

title: Balaram Jayanti
description: Lord Balaram appeared as the son of Mother Rohini and Vasudeva. His auspicious appearance day is celebrated as Balaram Jayanti which also known as Balaram Purnima.

title: Ratha Yatra Festival
description: The Rath Yatra celebration is an exuberant chariot festival dedicated to Lord Jagannatha, his elder brother Lord Baldeva, and his sister Devi Subhadra. During the procession in Rath Yatra Jaipur, Lord Jagannath graciously comes out of the temple to bless those who are unable to visit for His darshan.

title: Buddha Purnima
description: Lord Buddha preached the preliminary principles of the Vedas in a manner suitable for the time being (and so also did Sankaracarya) to establish the authority of the Vedas.

title: Kurma Jayanti
description: Kurma Jayanti is the appearance day of Lord Kurma, the second incarnation of Lord Vishnu.

title: Patotsav
description: Hare Krishna Movement Jaipur commemorates 13 year of service to the Lord and society.

title: Akshaya Tritiya
description: Akshaya Tritiya stands out as a profoundly auspicious occasion, ideal for embarking on new journeys.

title: Hanuman Jayanti
description: Hanuman Jayanti is the celebration of the auspicious appearance day of Sri Hanuman, an ardent devotee and eternal servitor of Lord Sri Ramachandra.

title: Sri Ram Navami
description: Sri Rama Navami is the auspicious appearance day of Lord Sri Ramachandra.

title: Sri Gaura Poornima
description: Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu appeared in Mayapur, Nadia, during a lunar eclipse, inspiring ecstatic devotion among the townspeople.

title: Nityanand Trayodashi
description: (Fasting till noon) Celebrate the divine appearance of Lord Nityananda, the eternal associate of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, who spreads love and devotion across the universe.

title: Gita Jayanti
description: Gita Jayanti is the auspicious day of the advent of Srimad Bhagavad-gita.

title: Govardhana Puja
description: Govardhana Puja is celebrated in the month of Kartika (October – November) to commemorate the pastime of Lord Sri Krishna lifting the Govardhana Hill to protect the residents of Vrindavana from the wrath of Indra.

title: Dusshera
description: In the Treta Yuga, the Supreme Lord appeared as Lord Rama, the son of Dasaratha. He was exiled, and His wife Sita (the daughter of King Janaka) and brother Lakshmana accompanied Him.

title: Vamana Jayanti
description: Vamana Jayanti is the appearance day of Lord Vamana. The Supreme Lord appeared as the son of Kashyapa and Aditi in the form of a dwarf Brahmana (Vamana) to deliver Bali Maharaja, a great devotee born in the family of demons.

title: Radha Ashtami
description: Sri Radhasthami is the auspicious appearance day of Srimati Radharani. The Vedic literatures state, Srimati Radharani is the universal Mother of all living entities.

title: Vyas Puja
description: Vyas Puja is a celebration to commemorate the appearance of Bonafide spiritual master.

title: Indira Ekadashi
description: (Full Day Fasting from Grains) Celebrated in the Krishna Paksha of Ashwin, this holy day involves fasting and worshiping Lord Vishnu to remove sufferings and solve problems.

title: Pashankusha Ekadashi
description: (Full Day Fasting from Grains) Pashankusha Ekadashi celebrated in the dark fortnight of Ashwin month after the Navratras.

title: Rama Ekadashi
description: (Full Day Fasting from Grains) According to Padma Purana, by observing this auspicious Ekadashi fast during the bright phase of the moon in Kartik, the devotee becomes purified and all desires are fulfilled.

title: Utthana Ekadashi
description: (Full Day Fasting from Grains) Falling on the 11th lunar day of the bright fortnight in Kartik, Utthana Ekadashi marks the end of Vishnu's four-month rest, celebrated with prayers and devotion.

title: Utpanna Ekadashi
description: (Full Day Fasting from Grains) Falls on 11th day of Krishna paksha in the month of Margashirsha, marks the appearance of devi Ekadashi.

title: Mokshada Ekadashi
description: (Full Day Fasting from Grains) Moshada Ekadashi, also known as Gita Jayanti, commemorates Lord Krishna’s revelation of the Gita to Arjuna in Kurukshetra. Observing this fast is believed to bring liberation and spiritual upliftment.

title: Shat-Tila Ekadashi
description: (Full Day Fasting from Grains) It is Observed on Krishna Paksha in Magh, Shat-Tila Ekadashi is revered for its profound spiritual significance.

title: Bhaimi Ekadashi
description: (Full Day Fasting from Grains) Bhaimi Ekadashi, falls on the 11th day of Shukla Paksha in Magha (January–February), is highly auspicious for fasting and devotional activities to please Lord Shri Krishna.

title: Vijaya Ekadashi
description: (Full Day Fasting from Grains) Vijaya Ekadashi, celebrated during the Krishna Paksha of Phalgun (February–March), is a day to seek blessings of the Supreme Lord for prosperity and victory in life.

title: Amalaki Ekadashi
description: (Full Day Fasting from Grains) Vijaya Ekadashi falls on the 11th day of the waxing moon in Phalguna (February-March), honors the amalaka tree, or Indian gooseberry, symbolizing divine blessings and prosperity.

title: Papamochani Ekadashi
description: Please Lord Vishnu by Observing Papmocani Ekadashi with Selfless Donation. Contribute and Get Freedom from All the Sins and Live a Peaceful and Happy Life ahead.

title: Kamada Ekadashi
description: As the Kamada Ekadashi Approaches, Seize the Auspicious Occasion to make a Meaningful Impact through your Generous Donation. Fulfill All Desires and obtain Spiritual Rewards by Embracing the Spirit of Giving.

title: Varuthini Ekadashi
description: Be Protected from All Evil with your Generous Donation. Contribute on the Auspicious Varuthini Ekadashi and Invoke Good Fortune.

title: Mohini Ekadashi
description: Remove the Darkest Illusory Attachments by Contributing on this Sacred Day. Donate for Mohini Ekadashi Day and Sow the Seeds of Blessings.

title: Apara Ekadashi
description: Donate on the Auspicious Apara Ekadashi Day. Draw the Divine Blessings of becoming Famous All Over the Universe with your Selfless Contribution.

title: Pandava Ekadashi
description: Nirjala Ekadashi is a sacred Hindu observance celebrated on the eleventh lunar day (Ekadashi) of the Shukla Paksha, the waxing phase of the moon, during the Hindu month of Jyeshtha.

title: Yogini Ekadashi
description: Secure Joy and Prosperity on the Fortunate Yogini Ekadashi Day. Donate Generously and Attract the Divine Blessings.

title: Shayani Ekadashi
description: Donate on the Auspicious Shayani Ekadashi and Nullify even the Worst Sins to become free of All Kinds of Disturbances. Contribute Generously to Receive Spiritual Blessings.

title: Kamika Ekadashi
description: Kamika Ekadashi, observed during the Krishna Paksha of Shravan, is a sacred day dedicated to Lord Vishnu and Tulasi. It is believed to remove sins and grant liberation.

title: Pavitropana Ekadashi
description: Observe Pavitropana Ekadashi with Meritorious Act of Charity. Donate and Receive Divine Blessings of Lord Vishnu on the Auspicious Day.

title: Annada Ekadashi
description: Ascend in Spiritual Life with your Devotional Contribution. Donate on the Propitious Annada Ekadashi Day and Vanquish All Miseries and Sufferings.

title: Parshva Ekadashi
description: Donate on the Opportune Parshva Ekadashi to attain All Kinds of Happiness. Cleans Heart of All Sinful Reactions and Easily Achieve Liberation with Generous Contribution.

title: Tulsi Shaligram Vivah
description: Celebrate Tulsi Shaligram Vivah with an Unselfish Contribution. Support Divine Festivities, Fostering Spiritual Joy, and Amplifying Krishna Consciousness.

title: Diwali
description: Contribute to Celebrate the Arrival of Lord Sri Ramcandra. Your Donation Brighten the Festivities and Serves the Community.

title: Dhanteras
description: Donate to Increase Wealth and Prosperity Today. Bring Good Luck in Your Life by invoking Divine Grace of Lord Sri Ramcandra.

title: Raksha Bandhan
description: Raksha bandhan festival marks the auspicious occassion of strengthening the care and protection bond in relations.

title: Srila Jiva Goswami - Appearance
description: Today we honor the Appearance of Srila Jiva Goswami, who was blessed by Mahaprabhu from childhood and was destined to become a prominent Acharya in the Gaudiya tradition.

title: Srila Bhaktivinod Thakur - Disappearance
description: On September 2, 1838, Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur, born Kedarnath Datta in Biranagara, appeared in opulence to revitalize the Hare Krishna Movement.

title: Srila Prabhupada Sannyasa Diwas
description: We honor the day Srila Prabhupada took sannyasa, guided by divine dreams and unwavering dedication, to spread Krishna consciousness globally despite many challenges.

title: Vijay Dashmi
description: On the tenth day of Asvina month , Vijayotsava commemorates Lord Ramachandra's joyous festival upon discovering Sita’s location in Sri Lanka. The celebration includes the dramatic burning of Ravana effigies and festive chants of ''Victory to Ram''.

title: Durga Puja
description: This festival marks the victory of Goddess Durga over the demon Mahishasura, celebrating her strength.

title: Sri Madhavacharya - Appearance
description: Today is the appearance day of Sri Madhavacharya, a prominent acharya in the Brahma-Sampradaya, who taught valuable lessons through his life.

title: Srila Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami Disappearance
description: Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami, one of the six Goswamis, gave up his wife and home to join Lord Caitanya’s sankirtana movement, showing true devotion and sacrifice.

title: Srila Raghunatha Batha Gosvami Disappearance
description: Raghunatha Bhatta Goswami, a prominent Goswami of Vrndavana, was directed by Lord Caitanya to chant the Hare Krsna mantra constantly, emphasizing the power of devotional chanting.

title: Srila Krishna Dasa Kaviraj Gosvami - Disappearance
description: Krishna Dasa Kaviraja, born near Katva, went to Vrindavana after a dream from Lord Nityananda, who assured him that his desires would be fulfilled. His is the author of "Caitanya Charitamrita".

title: Sri Krsna Saradiya Rasayatra
description: This event marks Lord Krsna's autumn rasa dance with His beloved gopis, celebrating divine love and joy during the festive season.

title: Laksmi Puja
description: This festival celebrates the worship of Laksmi Devi, the consort of Lord Vishnu. She is honored on Diwali, as she emerged from the ocean of milk, and devotees offer prayers and worship each year.

title: Disappearance Day of Sri Murari Gupta
description: Murari Gupta was a devoted associate of Lord Caitanya, serving Him throughout the Lord's pastimes in Navadvipa, showcasing deep love and dedication.

title: Kartik Month Begins
description: This month is the most auspicious and especially beloved by Lord Krishna, focusing on devotion and worship.

title: Navaratri Sthapana
description: This annual Hindu festival honors Goddess Durga, the protector and maintainer of whole material creation.

title: Srila Narottama Dasa Thakura - Disappearance
description: Srila Narottama Dasa Thakura, a prominent acarya, was the only disciple of Srila Lokanatha Gosvami, spreading the Gosvamis' teachings.

title: Beginning of 1st month of Chaturmasya
description: (Abstain from Green leafy vegetables) The Chaturmasya period begins in Ashadha (June-July). During Shravana, devotees should avoid eating spinach for spiritual upliftment.

title: Appearance Day of Radha Kunda, Snana Dana
description: This day celebrates the appearance of Radha Kunda, where devotees bathe at midnight on this day for blessings.

title: Bahulastami
description: On the eighth day of Damodara month, a beautiful pastime where the cow Bahula takes shelter of Krishna.

title: Srila Virabhadra Appearance
description: Srila Virabhadra Goswami appeared on the ninth day of the dark fortnight in Kartika month.

title: Bhai Dooj
description: Celebrated on the 2nd day of Kartik's bright fortnight, this festival honors the bond of love between brothers and sisters.

title: Kartik Purnima
description: Observed on the full moon day in Kartik, this renowned festival holds great significance in Hindu tradition and rituals.

title: Kansa Vadh
description: Celebrated on the 10th day of Kartik, this festival marks Lord Krishna's victory over Kansa and the restoration of King Ugrasena.

title: Chhath Puja
description: Celebrated six days after Diwali, this ancient festival honors the Sun God and expresses gratitude for sustaining life on Earth.

title: Sri Rasikananda - Appearance
description: Sri Rasikananda Prabhu, son of a king, became a sage and devoted disciple of Sri Syamananda Prabhu.

title: Bali Daityaraja Puja
description: This festival commemorates Bali Maharaja's surrender to Lord Vamanadeva, celebrated by worshiping the Deity of Vamana.

title: Sri Vasudeva Ghosh Disappearance
description: An intimate associate of Lord Caitanya, he was renowned for his powerful kirtana that moved even stone and wood, inspiring devotion among all.

title: Srila Prabhupada - Disappearance
description: (Fasting till noon) Devotees commemorate the disappearance of Srila Prabhupada, through heartfelt remembrances and readings from his biography.

title: Sri Gadadhara Dasa Goswami - Disappearance
description: Known for his deep devotion, Sri Gadadhara Dasa was an incarnation of Radharani’s effulgence and an expansion of Purnananda gopi.

title: Sri Dhananjaya Pandita Disappearance
description: Dhananjaya Pandita participated in Lord Caitanya’s kirtanas and traveled widely to preach Krishna consciousness.

title: Sri Srinivasa Acharya - Disappearance
description: Srinivasa Acharya helped bring the books of the six Goswamis from Vrindavan to Bengal and Orissa.

title: Gopastami
description: This day marks when Lord Krishna first grazed the cows, becoming a cowherd after caring for calves.

title: Jagaddhatri Puja
description: Worship of Jagaddhatri, a form of Mahamaya, occurs on this day, symbolizing the sustainer of the material world. (Vaisnavas do not usually observe this festival.)

title: Akshaya Navami
description: Observed on the 9th day of Kartik's bright fortnight, Akshaya Navami is considered as auspicious as Akshaya Tritiya.

title: Bhisma Pancaka
description: Bhisma Pancaka is a five-day fast observed in Kartik’s final days, beginning on Ekadasi and ending on Rasa Purnima.

title: Srila Gaura Kishora Dasa Disappearance
description: (Fasting till noon today in addition to regular Ekadashi fasting. Next day Feast after Sunrise) Srila Gaura Kishora Dasa Babaji Maharaja, well known as "Vairagya Murti" and a prominent acharya in the Gaudiya Vaishnava Sampradaya, was the spiritual master of Bhakti Siddhanta Sarasvati Maharaja.

title: Sri Bhugarbha Goswami Disappearance
description: Bhugarbha Goswami discovered Vrndavana’s lost holy sites on Lord Sri Chaitanya’s order with Lokanatha Goswami.

title: Sri Kasisvara Pandita Disappearance
description: Kasisvara Pandita served Lord Caitanya as a bodyguard and distributed prasadam after kirtans.

title: Sri Nimbarkacharya - Appearance
description: Nimbarkacharya, a prominent acharya of Kumara sampradaya, taught Krishna consciousness. (Before Lord Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu).

title: Dev Diwali
description: Dev Diwali, celebrated on Kartika Purnima, is the ‘Festival of Lights of the Gods’ in Varanasi.

title: Katyayani Vrata Begins
description: This vow involves austerities performed by the gopis to please Katyayani Devi for the blessing of marrying Lord Krishna, reflecting deep devotion and longing.

title: Vrischika Sankranti
description: Vrischika Sankranti is a propitious day for Shradh and Pitru Tarpan, honoring ancestors and seeking divine blessings.

title: Srila Prabhupada Diksha Diwas
description: On this auspicious day, Srila Prabhupada received initiation from his spiritual master, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura, at the Allahabad Gaudiya Math.

title: Sri Saranga Thakura Disappearance Day
description: Sri Saranga Thakura was an intimate associate of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. He resided under a Bakula tree in Navadvipa and was the disciple of the renowned devotee, Murari Thakura, known for his deep devotion.

title: Sri Kaliya Krishna Dasa Disappearance Day
description: Kaliya Krishna Dasa is noted as a disciple of Gauridasa Pandita, serving in the tradition of Lord Chaitanya and contributing to the spread of Krishna Consciousness.

title: Sri Narahari Sarakara Thakura Disappearance Day
description: Sri Narahari Sarakara was a personal associate of Lord Caitanya, known for his dedicated service, often fanning the Lord with a camara. He was also a great scholar and poet, contributing significantly to the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition.

title: Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura – Disappearance
description: (Fasting Till Noon) This day honors the disappearance of Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Sarasvati Thakura, the spiritual master of Srila Prabhupada.

title: Katyayani Vrata Ends
description: This day signifies the completion of Katyayani Vrata by the gopis seeking Krishna's blessings.

title: Srila Lochana Dasa Thakura Appearance
description: Srila Lochana Dasa Thakura appeared to propagate the teachings of Lord Chaitanya, remembered for devotional songs and contribution to bhakti literatures.

title: Sri Krishna Pushya Abhisheka
description: Sri Krishna Pushya Abhisheka celebrates the bathing and decorating of the Deity with ghee, flowers, and ornaments, followed by feasting and a festive procession for all to see Krishna's divine beauty.

title: Srila Ramchandra Kaviraj - Disappearance
description: On this day, we honor Srila Ramchandra Kaviraj's departure, a dear disciple of Srinivasa Acharya, celebrating his profound contributions to Krishna consciousness.

title: Srila Jayadeva Goswami Disappearance
description: On this day, we honor the disappearance of Srila Jayadeva Goswami, renowned for his poetic genius and deep devotion to Radha and Krishna through his masterpiece, Gita Govinda.

title: Srila Lochana Dasa Thakur Disappearance
description: On this day, we remember Srila Lochana Dasa Thakur's departure, a devoted disciple of Narahari Sarkar, who composed the esteemed "Chaitanya Mangala."

title: Srila Gopala Bhatta Goswami - Appearance
description: Srila Gopala Bhatta Goswami, a devoted disciple of Mahaprabhu, appeared in 1503, in a family of physicians in South India, destined for devotion.

title: Lohri
description: Lohri, also known as Lohadi or Lal Loi, is a festival closely related to Makar Sankranti, celebrating the harvest of rabi crops, especially sugarcane. For Punjabi farmers, Lohri marks the financial New Year.

title: Makar Sankranti
description: Makar Sankranti marks the sun's transition from Sagittarius to Capricorn, symbolizing new beginnings. Celebrated across India, it honors the solar deity Surya, and includes charity and daan as important traditions.

title: Srila Rasikananda - Disappearance
description: Srila Rasikananda, known for his exceptional qualities and miraculous preaching, attained his eternal pastimes, enriching the spiritual legacy of Gaudiya Vaishnavism.

title: Srila Jagannath Dasa Babaji - Disappearance
description: His disappearance marked a significant moment in the Vaishnava community, remembered for his profound contributions to the teachings of Lord Chaitanya.

title: Shiv Ratri
description: A significant night honoring Lord Shiva, observed with fasting, prayers, and devotion, culminating in blessings and spiritual growth.

title: Srila Ishvara Puri - Disappearance
description: A revered disciple of Madhavendra Puri, he profoundly influenced the path of devotion and was honored by Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

title: Srila Purushottama Dasa Thakura - Disappearance
description: A devoted disciple of Nityananda Prabhu, he exemplified selfless service and playful devotion to Lord Krishna.

title: Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura - Appearance
description: (Fasting till noon) Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Sarasvati Thakura's appearance is a significant occasion for devotees. He inspired many, including Srila Prabhupada, to spread the teachings of Lord Chaitanya.

title: Srila Narottama Dasa Thakura - Appearance
description: Srila Narottama Dasa Thakura, also known as Thakura Mahasaya, was a revered Gaudiya Vaishnava Acharya appeared in 1520 AD. He played a crucial role in spreading Vaishnava bhakti throughout Odisha and Bengal.

title: Sri Krishna Madhura Utsav
description: Sri Krishna Madhura Utsav celebrates Lord Krishna's rasa lila, marking the second full moon of Damodara month. This festival is particularly prominent in Bengal.

title: Varaha Dvadashi
description: On Varaha Dvadashi, devotees remember Lord Varaha Deva, who rescued the Earth from Hiranyaksha’s clutches.

title: Sri Ramanujacharya - Disappearance
description: Sri Ramanujacharya, an incarnation of Lakshman (Younger Brother of Lord Ramchandra), transcended the mortal realm, leaving a profound legacy in the realm of devotional philosophy and spiritual practice.

title: Sri Madhavacharya - Disappearance
description: Sri Madhavacharya, an incarnation of Vayu, founded the Dvaita philosophy and composed 37 significant texts, promoting devotion to Lord Krishna.

title: Bhishmashtami
description: Bhishma, originally named Devavrata, took a vow of celibacy and earned the name Bhishma, ensuring his father’s happiness.

title: Sri Advaita Acharya - Appearance
description: Sri Advaita Acharya, a combined incarnation of Maha Vishnu and Sada Shiva, appeared on the seventh day of the bright fortnight in Magh, enriching the world with devotion.

title: Vasanta Panchami
description: Vasanta Panchami celebrates the arrival of spring, with devotees offering yellow flowers and fresh grasses to Krishna, symbolizing new life and growth.

title: Saraswati Puja
description: Saraswati Puja honors the goddess of learning, where devotees pray for wisdom and understanding, offering books and flowers at her feet.

title: Srimati Vishnupriya Devi Appearance
description: Srimati Vishnupriya Devi, the beloved consort of Lord Gauranga, embodies devotion and grace in Gaudiya Vaishnavism.

title: Srila Vishvanatha Chakravarti Thakura - Disappearance
description: Commemorate Srila Vishvanatha Chakravarti Thakura's disappearance, reflecting on his life dedicated to spiritual practice and devotion to Lord Krishna.

title: Srila Raghuanatha Dasa Goswami - Appearance
description: Honoring Raghunatha Dasa Goswami's appearance, who cherished and served Shri Radharani with unwavering devotion throughout his life.

title: Sri Pundarika Vidyanidhi - Appearance
description: As an intimate friend of Svarupa Damodara, Pundarika Vidyanidhi played a vital role in the Vaishnava community, exemplifying pure devotion.

title: Srila Prabhupada - Appearance
description: (Fasting till noon) Srila Prabhupada appeared on the day of Nandotsav, a day just after Janmashtami.

title: Ananta Chaturdashi Vrata
description: In Bhadrapada, Chaturdashi date of Shukla Paksha is called Anant Chaturdashi. On the day of Anant Chaturdashi, Lord Vishnu, Mother Yamuna and Sheshnag are worshiped, and Anant Sutra is tied on this day.

title: Chandana Yatra Starts
description: This day marks the beginning of Chandan Yatra which continues for 21 days

title: Chandan Yatra Ends
description: This day marks the Completion of Chandan Yatra

title: Damanakaropana Dvadashi
description: This Festival is observed in Jagannath Puri, celebrated on the thirteenth and fourteenth days of the bright fortnight of Chaitra (April).

title: Sri Purushottama Dasa Thakura - Appearance
description: Commemorate the appearance of Sri Purusottama Dasa Thakura, a devoted servant of Lord Nityananda, immersed in divine pastimes.

title: Sri Madhavendra Puri - Disappearance
description: Commemorate the disappearance of Madhavendra Puri, whose ecstatic love and divine connection with Nityananda transformed holy places throughout India.

title: Jagannatha Mishra Festival
description: Jagannatha Mishra, father of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, held a grand festival for his divine appearance, similar to Nand Maharaj's celebrations for Krishna.

title: Sri Shrivasa Pandita - Appearance
description: Sri Srivasa Pandit, a prominent devotee and intimate associate of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, appeared to spread the holy name and foster devotion.

title: Sri Govinda Ghosh - Disappearance
description: The disappearance of Sri Govinda Ghosh marks a profound moment, as his unwavering devotion and service to Chaitanya Mahaprabhu continue to inspire devotees.

title: Matsya Jayanti
description: Celebrate Matsya Jayanti, honoring Lord Vishnu's first incarnation as the fish, who saved humanity from the great flood and protected sacred scriptures.

title: Ugadi Festival
description: Ugadi marks the New Year for many South Indians, celebrating the arrival of spring with vibrant festivities, traditional dishes, and the promise of new beginnings.

title: Rang Panchami
description: Rang Panchami is a Hindu festival celebrated five days after Holi, marking the arrival of spring. It occurs on the Panchami (5th day) of the Krishna Paksha in Chaitra month, usually falling in March.

title: Gangaur Vrat
description: Gangaur Vrat is a vibrant Hindu festival celebrating marital love, dedicated to Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati, primarily observed in Rajasthan.

title: Holika Dahan
description: Holika Dahan celebrates the victory of good over evil with bonfires symbolizing Holika's defeat by Lord Vishnu's grace.

title: Sri Ramanujacharya - Appearance
description: Sri Ramanujacharya, a key philosopher-saint of Sri Vaishnavism, revitalized Hindu philosophy and religion. Celebrated for his insight and devotion, he founded 'Ramanuja Darsanam,' influencing many aspects of Hinduism.

title: Sri Shyamananda Prabhu - Appearance
description: Shri Shyamananda Prabhu, a divine associate of Shri Gauranga, incarnated to spread Gaura-Krishna's teachings, showcasing remarkable devotion and intellect.

title: Sri Vansivadananda Thakura - Appearance
description: Sri Vansivadananda Thakura, Krishna's flute incarnation, appeared in Kuliya, serving Visnupriya and bringing Mahaprabhu's Deity to Navadwip.

title: Sharad Rasa Yatra
description: Devotees commemorate Sharad Rasa Yatra by offering sweet rice and performing special worship of Radha and Krishna amidst the gopis. (Sri Krishna Vasant Rasa)

title: Sri Gadadhara Dasa Goswami - Appearance
description: Shri Gadadhara Pandita embodied humility, patience, and unwavering devotion, often absorbed in the recitation of Srimad Bhagavatam.

title: Mesha Sankranti
description: Mesha Sankranti marks the Sun's transition into Aries, beginning the Hindu lunisolar New Year in Vaishakha.

title: parashuram Jayanti
description: Parashurama Jayanti, coinciding with Akshaya Tritiya, marks Lord Vishnu’s sixth incarnation, a day for enhanced rituals and charity.

title: jahnu Saptami
description: Jahnu Saptami honors Jahnu Muni, who swallowed and released the Ganga. Devotees bathe in and worship the sacred river.

title: Sri Madhu Pandita - Disappearance
description: Sri Madhu Pandita's devotion was so profound that Lord Gopinathji manifested before him, exemplifying the Lord's love for His devotees.

title: Srimati Sitadevi - Appearance
description: Sita Navami, or Sita Jayanti, celebrates the birth of Goddess Sita on the 9th day of Vaishaka's waxing moon phase.

title: Rukmini Dvadashi
description: Rukmini Dvadashi celebrates the appearance of Rukmini Devi, the beloved consort of Lord Krishna, known for their divine elopement.

title: Sri Jayananda Prabhu - Disappearance
description: Srila Prabhupada instructed to observe Jayananda Prabhu’s disappearance, recognizing his pure devotion and dedication to Krishna consciousness.

title: Sri Madhavendra Puri - Appearance
description: Nityananda Prabhu and Madhavendra Puri experienced overwhelming ecstatic love during their historic meeting in western India.

title: Sri Parameshvari Dasa Thakura - Disappearance
description: His Sripat features the deities of Shri Radha-Govinda, surrounded by two Bakul trees and Paramesvara Thakura's Samadhi mandira.

title: Sri Sri Radha-Ramana Devaji - Appearance
description: The grand temple of Shri Rangakshetra became a beacon of divine love, where devotees gathered to experience the mercy of Radha-Ramana.

title: Sri Srinivasa Acharya - Appearance
description: Shrinivasa Acharya was born in 1517 C.E., on the full moon day of the month of Vaishakha, in the village of Chakhandi.

title: Sri Ramananda Raya - Disappearance
description: Shri Ramananda Ray, the viceroy of the Godavari region, was a revered devotee and close associate of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

title: Ganga Saptami
description: Ganga Saptami honors Goddess Ganga's rebirth, celebrated on the 7th day of Vaishakha's waxing moon phase.

title: Srimati Jahnava Devi - Appearance
description: Srimati Jahnava Devi, beloved wife of Nityananda Prabhu, guided Gaudiya Vaishnavas with deep devotion.

title: Srila Vrindavana Dasa Thakura - Appearance
description: Born to Sri Narayani Devi, niece of Srivasa Pandita, he composed the "Sri Chaitanya Bhagavata." Narayani Devi received Mahaprabhu’s remnants, bestowing divine mercy upon her.

title: Narasimha Jayanti
description: Devotees observe fasting and perform rituals during sunset, emphasizing the importance of dharma and righteous living.

title: Vrishabha Sankranti
description: Vrishabha Sankranti marks the transition of the Sun from Aries to Taurus, initiating the second month of the Hindu solar calendar.

title: Shri Baladeva Vidyabhushana disappearance
description: Shrila Baladeva Vidyabhushana, a revered pure devotee, left his mortal frame, dedicating his life to serving humanity through literature.

title: Ganga Puja
description: This auspicious festival honors the birthday of Mother Ganges, symbolizing purity and spiritual cleansing for devotees across India.

title: Shrimati Gangamata Gosvamini appearance
description: Shrimati Gangamata Gosvamini, the daughter of King Naresanarayana, was deeply devoted to Madanagopala from a young age

title: Shri Mukunda Datta disappearance
description: Shri Mukunda Datta was born in Chanhara village, located in the Cattagrama district, about twenty miles from Pundarika Vidyanidhi's home.

title: Sri Sridhara Pandita disappearance
description: Sridhara's life and teachings continue to inspire devotees, reminding them of the power of sincere worship and dedication.

title: Panihati Chida Dahi Utsava
description: The Chida-dadhi Mahotsav celebrates the pastimes of Shrila Raghunatha dasa Goswami and Lord Nityananda Prabhu along the Ganges.

title: Jyeshtha Purnima / Devasnana Purnima
description: Devasnan Purnima celebrates the appearance day of Lord Jagannath with a special bathing ceremony on the full moon of Jyestha. (Snan Yatra)

title: Sri Shyamananda Prabhu - Disappearance
description: Sri Shyamananda Prabhu, Srinivasa Acharya, and Narottama dasa Thakura left this world, returning to their eternal abode.

title: Sri Vakreshvara Pandita - Appearance
description: Sri Vakreshwar Pandit was a devoted associate of Sriman Mahaprabhu, present during His pastimes in Navadwipa and Jagannath Puri.

title: Sri Shrivasa Pandita - Disappearance
description: Sri Shrivasa Pandita, a prominent associate of Lord Chaitanya, is revered for his deep devotion and service to the Lord.

title: Gundicha Marjana
description: Gundicha-marjana is the ritual cleaning of the Gundicha temple, performed to prepare for Lord Jagannath's arrival during Ratha Yatra.

title: Sri Svarupa Damodara Gosvami - Disappearance
description: Sri Swarup Damodar's disappearance is celebrated as a significant event among devotees, marking his eternal bond with Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

title: Sri Vakreshvara Pandita - Disappearance
description: Sri Vakreshwar Pandit’s disappearance is observed with reverence, marking the departure of a cherished devotee of Sriman Mahaprabhu.

title: Srila Haridasa Thakura - Disappearance
description: Srila Haridasa Thakura, deeply devoted to Hari Nama, left this world in Lord Chaitanya’s merciful presence.

title: Ganga Sagar Mela
description: Celebrated on Makar Sankranti, Ganga Sagar Mela brings pilgrims to bathe at the sacred Ganges-Bay of Bengal confluence.

title: Sri Raghunandana Thakura - Appearance
description: In Sri Khanda, Raghunandan’s sincere appeal moved Gopinath to accept his offering, a divine act that continues to inspire devotion in those who visit the deity.

title: Beginning of Tulasi Jala Dan
description: During Keshava Vrata, devotees cool Shaligram and Tulasi with dripping water for blessings.

title: Sri Abhirama Thakura - Disappearance
description: Revered associate of Nityananda Prabhu, Abhirama Thakura disappeared on Vaishakha Krishna Saptami.

title: Sri Balarama Rasayatra
description: During Caitra and Vaisakha, Balarama joyfully dances with Vrindavana's gopis to fulfill their desires.

title: Krishna Phula Dola
description: Krishna Phula Dola, also known as the Boat Festival, originates in Goloka Vrindavan, the spiritual realm where Lord Krishna eternally resides.

title: Salila Vihara
description: Salila Vihara is a summer festival celebrated for the pleasure of Sri Sri Radha-Krishna. The festival starts after Narsimha Caturdasi and continues for 15 days.

title: End of Tulasi Jala Dan
description: During Keshava Vrata, devotees cool Shaligram and Tulasi with dripping water for blessings.

title: Sri Gadadhara Pandita - Disappearance
description: Sri Gadadhara was the consant companion of Mahaprabhu from the time of their childhood. His father's name was Sri Madhva Mishra and his mother's name Sri Ratnavati Devi.

title: Sri Shivananda Sena - Disappearance
description: Sri Shivananda Sena was a Vaidya by caste. He lived in Kumarahatta at Halisahara. Shivananda had three sons named Chaitanyadasa, Ramadasa, and Paramanandadasa (Kavi Karnapura).

title: Hera Panchami
description: Hera Panchami ritual is an integral part of the Rath Yatra in Puri, is a captivating tradition where Goddess Laxmi expresses her anger towards Lord Jagannath by damaging his chariot, Nandighosha.

title: Ratha Yatra (Return)
description: This grand procession marks the journey of the deities from Gundicha Temple back to the Jagannath Temple.

title: Srila Gopala Bhatta Goswami - Disappearance
description: Sri Gopala Bhatta Goswami, one of the six Goswami(s) of Vrindavana. Gopala Bhatta Goswami established the Radha-Ramana Temple in Vrindavana.

title: The incorporation of ISKCON in New York
description: On July 29, 1966, A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada and his early disciples signed the incorporation documents, thus formally establishing ISKCON.

title: Srila Lokanatha Goswami - Disappearance
description: Srila Lokanatha Goswami disappeared on the day of Krishnashtami in the month of Sridhara.

title: Sri Vamshidasa Babaji - Disappearance
description: Sri Vamshidasa Babaji disappeared on the Gaura Chaturthi of Sridhara month.

title: Sri Raghunandana Thakura - Disappearance
description: According to Hindu lunar calendar Sri Raghunandana Thakura was disappeared on Gaura Paksha Chaturthi in Shravana (Sridhara) lunar month.

title: Srila Sanatana Goswami - Disappearance
description: Srila Sanatana Goswami is one of the six Goswami(s) of Vrindavana.

title: Guru (Vyasa) Purnima
description: This day marks the birthday of Veda Vyasa, the sage who authored the Mahabharata and compiled the Vedas.

title: Lalita Shashthi
description: Srimati Lalita Devi, foremost of all dearmost sakhis of Srimati Radharani appeared on shukla paksha shashti tithi in the month of Bhadrapada (Just 2 days before Radha Ashtami).

title: Srila Prabhupada's Departure for the USA
description: On the 13th of August, 1965, just a few days before Janmastami and a few days before his sixty-ninth birthday, Srila Prabhupada boarded the cargo ship Jaladuta.

title: Radha Govinda Jhulana Yatra Begins
description: It is a festival to celebrate Radha Krishna's pastime of swinging on a golden swing everyday until Balarama-purnima.

title: Srimati Sita Thakurani - Appearance
description: According to Hindu lunar calendar Shrimati Sita Thakurani was disappeared on Gaura Paksha Panchami in Bhadrapada (Hrsikesa) lunar month.

title: Sri Gauridasa Pandita - Disappearance
description: Sri Gauridasa Pandita Goswami was disappeared in the month of Shridhara on the Gaura Dvadashi, the twelfth day of the waxing moon.

title: Srila Rupa Goswami - Disappearance
description: Srila Rupa Goswami was disappeared on the Gaura Dvadashi of Shridhara month.

title: Radha Govind Jhulana Yatra Ends
description: This Day Marks the end of the annual festival of Radha Govind Julan Yatra.

title: Srila Bhaktivinod Thakur - Appearance
description: Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur (1838-1914), born Kedarnath Datta, was a pioneering spiritual leader, a magistrate working in colonial India under British rule, a prolific preacher, writer, and poet.

title: Appearance of Radha Kunda
description: This day marks the auspicious appearance of Radha Kunda on Kartik Ashtami.

title: Snana Dana
description: The appearance anniversary of Radha- kunda, the bathing pond of Srimati Radharani in Vrndavana.

title: Sri Virabhadra - Appearance
description: Sri Virabhadra Prabhu appeared on the ninth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kartik.

title: Kartik Amavasya
description: The most important day in the Hindu calendar, Kartik Amavasya, corresponds to the new moon in the month of Kartika.

title: Krishna Balaram Shobha Yatra
description: A grand procession of Sri Sri Krishna Balram is organized every year by the Hare Krishna Movement with great joy and devotion.

title: Parshuram Jayanti
description: A divine day when Lord Parshuram was born, celebrate as Parshuram Jayanti, on 30th April, 2025. It is glorified across India to spread the devotion among devotees.

title: Padmini Ekadashi
description: Padmini Ekadashi, also known as Kamala Ekadashi, is the one religiously important festival in the Hindu calendar.

title: Parama Ekadashi
description: Parama Ekadashi is one of the most sacred Ekadashis in Hindu tradition. It is observed during the Krishna Paksha, the waning phase of the moon, in the auspicious Adhik Maas, also known as the extra lunar month.

title: Jyeshtha Amavasya
description: Jyeshtha Amavasya is a sacred day for prayers, charity, and offering seva for peace, purification, and blessings for ancestors.

title: Jyeshtha Adhika Purnima
description: On Adhika Purnima, offer seva with devotion and receive the blessings of Lord Krishna through Gau Seva, Annadan, and sacred charity.

title: Adhika Amavasya
description: On Adhika Amavasya, perform Gau Seva, Annadan, and devotional charity to seek Lord Krishna’s mercy and spiritual upliftment.

title: Ashadha Amavasya
description: Ashadha Amavasya is an auspicious day for remembrance, charity, and seva, helping devotees cultivate humility, gratitude, and spiritual strength.

title: Ashadha Purnima
description: On Ashadha Purnima, devotees honor spiritual wisdom, offer prayers, and perform seva to receive divine grace and inner purification.

title: Shravana Amavasya
description: Shravana Amavasya encourages devotees to offer prayers and charity, seeking divine blessings for family, ancestors, and spiritual progress.

title: Shravana Purnima Vrat
description: Shravana Purnima is a blessed occasion for worship, charity, and remembering the Lord with sincerity, purity, and devotional offerings.

title: Bhadrapada Amavasya
description: Bhadra Amavasya is a meaningful day for worship, charity, and devotional reflection, bringing peace to the heart and home

title: Bhadrapada Purnima
description: Bhadrapada Purnima inspires devotees to offer prayers, perform sacred charity, and seek Lord Krishna’s mercy for family and spiritual growth.

title: Ashwina Amavasya
description: Ashwina Amavasya is ideal for sacred offerings, ancestor prayers, and seva, helping devotees receive blessings and inner purification.

title: Ashwina Purnima Vrat
description: On Ashwina Purnima, devotees observe worship and charity, praying for divine blessings, peace, purity, and deeper connection with Lord Krishna.

title: Margashirsha Purnima
description: Margashirsha Purnima is a sacred full moon day dedicated to worship, charity, and spiritual practices. Devotees observe prayers, holy bathing, and devotion to Lord Vishnu on this auspicious occasion, believing it brings peace, prosperity, and spiritual blessings into life.

title: Margashirsha Amavasya
description: Margashirsha Amavasya is an important new moon day observed with prayers, charity, and rituals for ancestors. Many devotees perform holy bathing, offer donations, and worship Lord Vishnu and forefathers, believing it helps bring peace, spiritual growth, and positive energy.
